text:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PD-12456 — HIGH — gpu-node-12a (rack-7) kernel oops & reboot loop. Service: inference-serving-us-west-2.
pagerduty-bot: Trigger: kernel OOPS detected, machine rebooted 3x in last 8m. kubelet now NotReady. Alerts: increased 5xx rate for text-gen route /v1/generate in us-west-2 (~5% errors), latency p95 up 2x.

maria: ACK. I'm on it — switching laptop to SRE mode.
maria: quick note: gpu-node-12a hosts 4 inference pods (redwood-13b-v0) and 2 batch jobs. If it stays flapping we'll need to drain and failover.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation: if not ACK within 3m escalate to SRE-second.
devin: joining — on my way. any live customer reports?
maria: no direct CS tickets yet, but metrics match a small spike in 5xxs from a handful of orgs. tagging CS.

anita: FYI I got a webhook from monitoring: "node_reboot_count > 2 in 10m" for gpu-node-12a.

kai: can you paste the kubelet status and journalctl tail?
maria: running commands now:

```
kubectl get nodes gpu-node-12a -o wide
NAME           STATUS     ROLES   AGE   VERSION
gpu-node-12a   NotReady   <none>  72d   v1.28.4

kubectl describe node gpu-node-12a | egrep -A3 "Conditions|Addresses"
Conditions:
  KubeletNotReady  False  Reason: KernelOops
Addresses:
  InternalIP: 10.4.7.123
```

maria: journalctl -u kubelet --since "10 minutes ago" | tail -n 50:

```
Mar 12 15:02:01 gpu-node-12a kernel: [  123.456789] Kernel panic - not syncing: OOPS in module nvidia_driver
Mar 12 15:02:05 gpu-node-12a systemd[1]: Rebooting...
Mar 12 15:05:30 kubelet[1234]: Starting kubernetes kubelet...
Mar 12 15:05:42 kubelet[1234]: Failed to enable device plugin: nvidia driver not ready
Mar 12 15:07:58 kernel: [  345.678901] Kernel OOPS: stack overflow in process kworker/2:3
Mar 12 15:08:02 systemd[1]: Rebooting...
```

devin: looks like a hardware/driver level panic (nvidia). might be a bad driver/firmware or failing GPU. we should cordon+drain that host and re-schedule pods.

maria: agree. immediate mitigation plan:
- cordon gpu-node-12a
- drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data to move inference pods
- temporarily update routing to avoid scheduling new gen jobs on us-west-2 rack-7
- notify CS about degraded error rate and that we're failing over pods

kai: i'll take the drain if you want to coordinate, maria. runbook says ensure autoscaler has capacity for 4 pods.

maria: ok executing now:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12a
kubectl drain gpu-node-12a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

sre-bot: Note: Pod redwood-13b-v0-abcde failed to schedule within 90s; trying next node.

maria: pods rescheduled successfully to gpu-node-3b and gpu-node-9c. Live metrics: 5xx rate dropping from 5% -> 1.2% in last 3m.

anita: :thumbsup: good. should we also restart kube-proxy on the node or force a reprovision?
devin: given repeated kernel panics I'm leaning to hardware replacement or firmware rollback. ops-team should coordinate rack swap.

ops-bot: Created ticket OPS-7789: hardware replacement request for gpu-node-12a (rack-7). ETA 4h for tech on site (on-prem partner).

maria: tagging CS: @customer-success — we've failed over pods off gpu-node-12a and error rates are returning to normal. Potential impact window: ~15m. We'll update if customers report anything.
anita: can we also enable fallback routing for sensitive tenants to use smaller model (redwood-3b) for 10m to reduce risk?

maria: yes — doing a temporary routing rule.

```
# console change (rolling): route tenant-critical -> redwood-3b for us-west-2 for 10m
```

kai: while you did that, did you capture disk / dmesg? if there's a persistent hardware error we'll want logs for support.
maria: grabbing logs and snapshotting dmesg, uploading to incidents bucket.

```
dmesg | tail -n 80 > /tmp/gpu-node-12a-dmesg.log
aws s3 cp /tmp/gpu-node-12a-dmesg.log s3://redwood-incidents/1923456789/
```

devin: monitoring shows tail latency back to normal and error rate ~0.8%. I think mitigation worked. leaving a small watch for another 15m.

pagerduty-bot: PD-12456 status changed: acknowledged by maria at 2026-03-12T15:10:05Z.

maria: I'm going to hand this over to devin for the watch. Devin — i'll add notes and logs to the incident ticket.
devin: taking handoff. I'll be primary for the next 60m — will escalate to hardware if another panic occurs.

maria: handoff notes:
- root cause suspected: nvidia driver/kernel interaction -> kernel OOPS.
- mitigation: cordon+drain; routing changes; Ops ticket created for hardware replacement.
- customer impact: brief ~15m spike in 5xxs for /v1/generate in us-west-2 (~5% -> now <1%). No direct CS tickets at time of handoff.

anita: can we also add a temporary rule in the rollout manager to hard-fallback to redwood-3b for retriable 5xxs? avoids customer-facing errors.

kai: doing it now — added automatic fallback for 5xx > 1% for 5m windows.

devin: monitoring channel please watch for: repeated reboots on gpu-node-12a (if it comes back) and reappearance of 5xxs. I'll keep PD open for 60m.

sre-bot: Reminder: create postmortem if outage > 15m or customer impact reported.

maria: filing incident ticket INC-1923456789 with attachments and timeline.

ops-bot: OPS-7789 updated: tech on site confirmed GPU health failure; RMA in progress.

devin: all quiet for now. moving thread to watch state. will update before PD auto-close.

pagerduty-bot: PD-12456 will auto-resolve if no further alerts in 60 minutes.

maria: thanks everyone. I'll jump back in if anything noisy pops. :white_check_mark:

kai: nice runbook execution. logging follow-ups for kernel driver versions and deployment guidance.

anita: ping me if we need to notify any customer directly — CS standing by.

[END THREAD]"
